"AVATAR: THE FOUR ELEMENTS

Open-World RPG Adventure Game

Create a fully playable 3D open-world RPG inspired by the universe of Avatar: The Last Airbender.

The game takes place in a vast world inspired by the Four Nations: the Water Tribes, the Earth Kingdom, the Fire Nation, and the Air Nomads.

The player must be able to freely explore the world, discover villages, cities, temples, forests, mountains, oceans, caves, and ancient ruins.

1. Character Creation and Origins

At the beginning of the game, the player creates their own character.

Allow the player to customize:

- Name
- Gender
- Appearance
- Hairstyle and hair color
- Skin tone
- Clothing
- Starting nation
- Character background

The player must be born into one of the four nations.

Depending on their origin, they will have access to a different bending ability.

There are five possible character types:

- Waterbender
- Earthbender
- Firebender
- Airbender
- Avatar

The Avatar is extremely rare. If the player is born as the Avatar, they can eventually master all four elements.

If the player is not the Avatar, they can only master their native element.

2. Elemental Bending System

Create a dynamic elemental combat system with fluid animations and different abilities for each element.

Waterbending:

- Control water
- Create water whips
- Launch waves
- Freeze water into ice
- Create ice spikes
- Control large amounts of water
- Heal using waterbending

Earthbending:

- Raise walls and pillars
- Throw rocks at enemies
- Create earthquakes
- Open cracks in the ground
- Control large boulders
- Create stone armor

Firebending:

- Shoot fireballs
- Create fire streams
- Launch powerful explosions
- Perform fire kicks and punches
- Generate lightning (advanced ability)
- Redirect lightning (advanced ability)

Airbending:

- Create air blasts
- Generate powerful tornadoes
- Push enemies away
- Create air shields
- Glide using an air glider
- Perform aerial attacks

Each element must have its own skill tree, abilities, animations, and progression system.

3. Avatar System

If the player is born as the Avatar, they have a special progression system.

The Avatar starts with their native element and must learn the other three elements by finding masters around the world.

The Avatar can eventually unlock:

- All four elements
- Advanced bending techniques
- Avatar State
- Powerful elemental combinations

The Avatar State should be an extremely powerful temporary transformation that increases bending damage and ability strength.

4. Open World

Create a large, explorable world with four major nations.

Each nation must have:

- Unique architecture
- Different environments
- NPCs with daily routines
- Shops and merchants
- Trainers and bending masters
- Quests and side missions
- Hidden locations
- Enemies and dangerous creatures

The player can travel between nations using boats, air travel, mounts, and other transportation methods.

The world should feel alive, with a day-and-night cycle and changing weather.

5. Player HUD and Interface

Create a clean, beautiful RPG interface.

At the bottom of the screen, display:

Health Bar: Shows the player's current health.

Energy Bar: Represents the player's bending energy. Using bending abilities consumes energy, which regenerates over time.

Inventory: A visible inventory button that opens the player's backpack.

The inventory should contain:

- Weapons
- Clothing
- Food
- Potions
- Materials
- Quest items
- Collectibles

Also include:

- Player level
- Experience bar
- Current bending element
- Map
- Quest tracker
- Ability shortcuts

The HUD should remain visible while exploring and fighting.

6. Combat and Progression

Create real-time combat where the player can combine basic attacks, bending abilities, dodging, blocking, and special moves.

The player earns experience by:

- Defeating enemies
- Completing quests
- Exploring locations
- Training with masters
- Discovering secrets

Leveling up should unlock new abilities and (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-friendly Four Nations RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Character creation with name, identity, background, nation, and a rare Avatar option.
- Four elemental bending paths, exploration, combat, NPC/master interactions, quests, progression, inventory, map, and responsive touch controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Implement as a single-file, canvas-rendered 2D game with a painted/isometric-style world rather than 3D.
- Use original nation names and characters inspired by the requested setting.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with a visual layout, character-creation modal, HUD, inventory/map/journal modals, and mobile control styling.
- Added partial gameplay/rendering JavaScript for world scenery, combat, movement, skills, quests, and progression.

### Active
- Repair `index.html`: its current `<script>` starts at `drawEnemies()` and is missing required earlier JavaScript declarations/functions, so it will fail at runtime.
- Complete and validate the game in-browser, including a latest JPEG screenshot check.

### Blocked
- Game runtime is currently blocked by the incomplete JavaScript initialization; no post-repair syntax or browser tests have been run.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html`; add the missing setup code before `drawEnemies()` (DOM helpers, canvas/state initialization, render helpers such as `drawBackdrop`, nation data, player state, and other referenced functions).
2. Run a JavaScript syntax check, launch the app, and test character creation, movement, attacks, interactions, and overlays.
3. Save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot; fix any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Current game implementation; contains the interface and partial game logic.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A syntax-check attempt before the last edit failed because the expected `<script>` match was absent; no validation was performed afterward.
- The current `index.html` has the markup and script tail but not the initialization/setup code that the script references.
